inputs.text: I don’t buy the idea that legal safeguards are an obstacle to public safety. Giving the state broader surveillance powers without strong limits risks putting everyone—especially people already subject to discrimination or political scrutiny—under greater pressure, while asking the public to trust institutions with little accountability. With the bill due before the House plenum on Thursday, lawmakers should explain exactly what powers it grants and make meaningful oversight and protections central. Security matters, but it cannot be used to sideline rights or treat scrutiny as a threat.

output.main_topic: Concerns that broader state surveillance powers could undermine rights without strong safeguards and oversight
subtopics: Pressure on people subject to discrimination or political scrutiny
